34988-the-professor-s-mystery.title: Mystery
34988-the-professor-s-mystery.creator: Wells Hastings
34988-the-professor-s-mystery.description: A book by Wells Hastings. At this point I believe I swore. At least I have no recollection of not doing so, and I should hardly have forgotten so eminent an act of virtue under such difficult circumstances. It was not only that I had worked myself into a heat for nothing.

arxiv-2010-10994.title: On Random Subset Generalization Error Bounds and the Stochastic Gradient Langevin Dynamics Algorithm
arxiv-2010-10994.creator: Borja Rodríguez-Gálvez, Germán Bassi, Ragnar Thobaben, Mikael Skoglund
arxiv-2010-10994.description: Abstract In this work, we unify several expected generalization error bounds based on random subsets using the framework developed by Hellström and Durisi 2020 . First, we recover the bounds based on the individual sample mutual information from Bu et al. 2020 and on a random subset of the dataset from Negrea et al. 2019 .

arxiv-2102-11052.title: Bose-Einstein Condensation with Optimal Rate for Trapped Bosons in the Gross-Pitaevskii Regime
arxiv-2102-11052.creator: Christian Brennecke, Benjamin Schlein, Severin SchravenDepartment of Mathematics, Harvard University, One Oxford Street, Cambridge MA 02138, USAInstitute of Mathematics, University of Zurich, Winterthurerstrasse 190, 8057 Zurich, Switzerland
arxiv-2102-11052.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Christian Brennecke, Benjamin Schlein, Severin SchravenDepartment of Mathematics, Harvard University, One Oxford Street, Cambridge MA 02138, USAInstitute of Mathematics, University of Zurich, Winterthurerstrasse 190, 8057 Zurich, Switzerland. We consider a Bose gas consisting of N N particles in ℝ 3 \mathbb{R}^{3} , trapped by an external field and interacting through a two-body potential with scattering length of order N − 1 N^{-1} .

arxiv-2204-07788.title: A simple, passive design for large optical trap arrays for single atoms
arxiv-2204-07788.creator: P. Huft, Y. Song, T. M. Graham, K. Jooya, S. Deshpande, C. Fang, M. Kats, M. Saffman
arxiv-2204-07788.description: Abstract We present an approach for trapping cold atoms in a 2D optical trap array generated with a novel 4 ​ f 4f filtering scheme and custom transmission mask without any active device. The approach can be used to generate arrays of bright or dark traps, or both simultaneously with a single wavelength for forming two-species traps.

arxiv-2209-05530.title: Model-based Reinforcement Learning with Multi-step Plan Value Estimation
arxiv-2209-05530.creator: Haoxin Lin, Yihao Sun, Jiaji Zhang, Yang YuNational Key Laboratory for Novel Software Technology, Nanjing University, Nanjing, Jiangsu, China{linhx, sunyh, zhangjj}@lamda.nju.edu.cn, yuy@nju.edu.cn
arxiv-2209-05530.description: Abstract A promising way to improve the sample efficiency of reinforcement learning is model-based methods, in which many explorations and evaluations can happen in the learned models to save real-world samples. However, when the learned model has a non-negligible model error, sequential steps in the model are hard to be accurately evaluated, limiting the model’s utilization.

arxiv-2309-08442.title: Toward responsible face datasets: modeling the distribution of a disentangled latent space for sampling face images from demographic groups
arxiv-2309-08442.creator: Parsa Rahimi, Christophe Ecabert, Sébastien Marcel
arxiv-2309-08442.description: Abstract Recently, it has been exposed that some modern facial recognition systems could discriminate specific demographic groups and may lead to unfair attention with respect to various facial attributes such as gender and origin. The main reason are the biases inside datasets, unbalanced demographics, used to train theses models.

The Extra-Low ENergy Antiproton ring at CERN, commissioned at the AD in 2018, now supplies a bunch of electron-cooled antiprotons at a fixed energy of 100 keV.

arxiv-2404-06554.title: Deformations of exterior differential ideals and applications.
arxiv-2404-06554.creator: Fernando Cukierman, César Massri
arxiv-2404-06554.description: Abstract . We develop some basic facts on deformations of exterior differential ideals on a smooth complex algebraic variety. With these tools we study deformations of several types of differential ideals, leading to several irreducible components of the corresponding moduli spaces. 2010 Mathematics Subject Classification 14Mxx, 37F75, 32S65, 32G13. arxiv-2412-17913.title: Quantum entanglement of XY-type spin dimers in Shastry-Sutherland lattice
arxiv-2412-17913.creator: Qianli Ma ∗, Brianna R. Billingsley ∗, Madalynn Marshall, David A. Dahlbom, Yiqing Hao, Daniel M. Pajerowski, Alexander I. Kolesnikov, Xiaojian Bai, Cristian D. Batista, Tai Kong †, Huibo Cao †
arxiv-2412-17913.description: Abstract We report a comprehensive study on the origin of the enigmatic disordered ground state within the Shastry-Sutherland lattice, BaCe 2 ZnS 5 , at low temperatures. The magnetization and heat capacity data show a lack of magnetic ordering down to 73 mK.

arxiv-2501-11073.title: Poset probability in two-row partition posets
arxiv-2501-11073.creator: Albin Jaldevik, Jan Snellman
arxiv-2501-11073.description: Abstract We find explicit formulae for poset probabilities ℙ ⁡ ( P λ , α < β ) \mathbb{P}(P_{\lambda};\alpha<\beta) in partition posets (cell posets) P λ P_{\lambda} when λ = ( λ 1 , λ 2 ) \lambda=(\lambda_{1},\lambda_{2}) is a two-row partition.

arxiv-2504-00665.title: Monocular and Generalizable Gaussian Talking Head Animation
arxiv-2504-00665.creator: Shengjie Gong Haojie Li Jiapeng Tang Dongming Hu Shuangping Huang, Hao Chen Tianshui Chen Zhuoman Liu
arxiv-2504-00665.description: Abstract In this work, we introduce Monocular and Generalizable Gaussian Talking Head Animation (MGGTalk), which requires monocular datasets and generalizes to unseen identities without personalized re-training. Compared with previous 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) methods that requires elusive multi-view datasets or tedious personalized learning/inference, MGGtalk enables more practical and broader applications.

arxiv-2508-11748.title: Hot, cold, and multi-component accretion flows around supermassive black hole binaries
arxiv-2508-11748.creator: Christopher Tiede, Daniel J. D’Orazio
arxiv-2508-11748.description: Abstract We develop a model for supermassive black hole binaries (SMBHBs) accreting below their Eddington limit, focusing on systems where hot, advection-dominated flows become viable. We specifically explore the spectral appearance of multi-component accretion flows where the solution can independently transition between cold, thin disks and hot, advection-dominated torii depending on the local accretion rate.

arxiv-2510-01948.title: ClustViT: Clustering-based Token Merging for Semantic Segmentation
arxiv-2510-01948.creator: Fabio Montello, Ronja Güldenring, Lazaros Nalpantidis
arxiv-2510-01948.description: Abstract Vision Transformers can achieve high accuracy and strong generalization across various contexts, but their practical applicability on real-world robotic systems is limited due to their quadratic attention complexity. Recent works have focused on dynamically merging tokens according to the image complexity. Token merging works well for classification but is less suited to dense prediction.

arxiv-2510-10021.creator: Euclid Collaboration: L. Blot, K. Tanidis, G. Cañas-Herrera, P. Carrilho, M. Bonici, S. Camera, V. F. Cardone, S. Casas, S. Davini, S. Di Domizio, S. Farrens, L. W. K. arxiv-2510-10021.description: Abstract Extracting cosmological information from the Euclid galaxy survey will require modelling numerous systematic effects during the inference process. This implies varying a large number of nuisance parameters, which have to be marginalised over before reporting the constraints on the cosmological parameters.

arxiv-2511-19504.title: Position: The Complexity of Perfect AI Alignment – Formalizing the RLHF Trilemma
arxiv-2511-19504.creator: Subramanyam Sahoo, Aman Chadha, Vinija Jain, Divya Chaudhary
arxiv-2511-19504.description: Abstract Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (RLHF) has become the dominant approach for aligning large language models, yet practitioners face a persistent puzzle: improving safety often reduces fairness, scaling to diverse populations becomes computationally intractable, and making systems robust often amplifies majority biases.

pmc-10569644.title: Proximity-dependent mapping of the HCMV US28 interactome identifies RhoGEF signaling as a requirement for efficient viral reactivation
pmc-10569644.creator: Samuel Medica, Lindsey B. Crawford, Michael Denton, Chan-Ki Min, Taylor A. Jones, Timothy Alexander, Christopher J. Parkins, Nicole L. Diggins, Gabriel J. Streblow, Adam T. Mayo, Craig N. Kreklywich, Patricia Smith, Sophia Jeng, Shannon McWeeney, Meaghan H. Hancock, Andrew Yurochko, Michael S. Cohen
pmc-10569644.description: Human cytomegalovirus (HCMV) encodes multiple putative G protein-coupled receptors (GPCRs). US28 functions as a viral chemokine receptor and is expressed during both latent and lytic phases of virus infection. US28 actively promotes cellular migration, transformation, and plays a major role in mediating viral latency and reactivation; however, knowledge about the interaction partners involved in these processes is still incomplete.

pmc-10590969.title: Self-evolved BOx anchored on Mg2B2O5 crystallites for high-performance oxidative dehydrogenation of propane
pmc-10590969.creator: Dake Zhang, Shenghua Wang, Xingyu Lu, Chengcheng Zhang, Kai Feng, Le He, Hui Zhang, Wei Sun, Deren Yang
pmc-10590969.description: SummaryOxidative dehydrogenation of propane (ODHP) is a promising process for producing propene. Recently, some boron-based catalysts have exhibited excellent olefin selectivity in ODHP. However, their complex synthetic routes and poor stability under high-temperature reaction conditions have hindered their practical application.

pmc-10720241.title: Social disparities and inequalities in healthcare access and expenditures among Iranians exposed to sulfur mustard: a national study using spatio-temporal analysis
pmc-10720241.creator: Seyed-Morteza Hosseini-Shokouh, Mostafa Ghanei, Batool Mousavi, Hassan Bagheri, Mohammadkarim Bahadori, Mohammad Meskarpour-Amiri, Parisa Mehdizadeh
pmc-10720241.description: Background Sulfur Mustard (SM) is a chemical warfare agent that has serious short-term and long-term effects on health. Thousands of Iranians were exposed to SM during the eight-year Iran-Iraq conflict and permanently injured while the socioeconomic imbalance in their healthcare utilization (HCU) and health expenditures remains.

pmc-10747835.title: Physical Noninvasive Attacks on Photoplethysmogram by Computer Controlled Blood Pressure Cuff
pmc-10747835.creator: Kazuki Yoshida, Ryota Sawano, Masahiro Okamoto, Kazuya Murao, Shuhei Tsuchida, Tsutomu Terada, Yvonne Tran
pmc-10747835.description: Sensor data has been used in social security and welfare infrastructures such as insurance and medical care to provide personalized products and services; there is a risk that attackers can alter sensor data to obtain unfair benefits. We consider that one of the attack methods to modify sensor data is to attack the wearer’s body to modify biometric information.

pmc-11351293.title: Building a predictive model for depression risk in fracture patients: insights from cross-sectional NHANES 2005–2020 data and an external hospital-based dataset
pmc-11351293.creator: Xin Liu, Xin Jin, Wujia Cen, Yi Liu, Shaoting Luo, Jia You, Sha Tian
pmc-11351293.description: BackgroundDepression represents a frequent mental health challenge in individuals with fractures, negatively impacting their recuperation and overall well-being. The purpose of this research was to formulate and corroborate a prognostic framework for pinpointing depression risk among fracture sufferers by utilizing data from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) from 2005 to 2020 and a separate hospital-based group.

pmc-11716124.title: Cardiorespiratory Fitness Modifies the Association Between Cerebral Pulsatility on Amyloid Burden and Core CSF Biomarkers of Alzheimer’s Disease
pmc-11716124.creator: Brianne M. Breidenbach, Talia L. Brach, Matthew P Glittenberg, Adam J Paulsen, Leah E Symanski, Tarun Naren, Ira Driscoll, Sarah R Lose, Catherine L. Gallagher, Sterling C. Johnson, Sanjay Asthana, Tobey J. Betthauser, Leonardo A. Rivera‐Rivera, Bruce P Hermann, Mark A. Sager, Kaj Blennow, Henrik Ze
pmc-11716124.description: BackgroundIncreasing evidence supports the notion that vascular dysfunction contributes to the evolution of Alzheimer’s disease (AD). Cerebral pulsatility index (PI) is reportedly higher in AD and MCI compared to age matched controls and has been associated with greater beta‐amyloid (Aß) burden. Higher cardiorespiratory fitness (CRF) positively affects vascular function and is associated with lower PI in several large cerebral vessels.

pmc-12422107.title: Shifts in clinical practice and patient demographics following the introduction of holmium laser enucleation for benign prostatic hyperplasia in a general urology clinic
pmc-12422107.creator: Ankur U Choksi, Shayan Smani, Soum D Lokeshwar, Vinaik M Sundaresan, Christopher S Hayden, Daniel A Segal, Daniel S Kellner
pmc-12422107.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Background:Holmium laser enucleation of the prostate (HoLEP) has emerged as an effective surgical treatment for benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH). This study evaluated how the adoption of HoLEP in a general urology clinic influenced clinical and procedural volume.Objective:To better understand the practice ramifications of HoLEP adoption, we analyzed the changes to a general urologist’s patient demographics and practice patterns after the addition of HoLEP to their surgical repertoire.Methods:We retrospectively reviewed the electronic health records 30 months before and after the introduction of HoLEP

pmc-13074347.title: Evidence of Antiproliferative Activity in the Liverwort Isotachis serrulata from Southern Ecuador
pmc-13074347.creator: José Miguel Andrade, Ángel Benítez, Aday González-Bakker, Luis Cartuche, José M. Padrón, Ana R. Díaz-Marrero, José J. Fernandez
pmc-13074347.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Natural products from bryophytes represent an underexplored source of structurally diverse bioactive compounds. In this study, extracts of Isotachis serrulata collected in southern Ecuador were evaluated for antiproliferative activity against five human tumor cell lines. Sequential extraction and chromatographic fractionation yielded six fractions, among which fraction IsF5 displayed the most notable activity, particularly against lung (SW1573) and breast (T-47D) cancer cell lines, with GI50 values within the moderate activity range according to National Cancer Institute criteria.

pmc-13107742.title: Mycobacterium tuberculosis infection disrupts gut and respiratory microbial communities and networks with incomplete restoration after two months of treatment
pmc-13107742.creator: Sohyoung Won, Juyong Hong, Heebal Kim, Junho Lee, Young Chun Ko, Bumhee Yang, Sun-Hyung Kim, Seok Shin Koh, Jeeyeon Park, Gee Oh Guak, Gyeong In Lee, Youngeun Choi, Seung Heon Lee, Gisu Kang, Seoae Cho, Hyejin Kim
pmc-13107742.description: Pulmonary tuberculosis (TB), caused by Mycobacterium tuberculosis (MTB), remains a major global health concern. Respiratory infections can influence the gut microbiome, and vice versa, through communication between the gut and respiratory microbiome—the gut–lung axis. Yet how TB infection and treatment relate to this connection remains unclear.

pmc-13541344.title: Central Diabetes Insipidus as a Rare Cause of Polyuria
pmc-13541344.creator: Stuti Bhandari, Samyama Sagare Venkatesh, L.U Chirag, Rajeev Gowda
pmc-13541344.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Central diabetes insipidus (CDI) is a rare condition characterized by arginine vasopressin deficiency, leading to persistent polyuria and polydipsia. Although it can present at any age, idiopathic CDI in young adults is uncommon and diagnostically challenging. Inflammatory conditions such as infundibuloneurohypophysitis must be considered, particularly when magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) reveals a thickened pituitary stalk and absence of the posterior pituitary bright spot. Early recognition and differentiation from diabetes mellitus, nephrogenic diabetes insipidus, and primary polydipsia are crucial for effective management.

pmc-13549946.title: Changing sea ice cover led to marine biodiversity shifts in the Late Quaternary
pmc-13549946.creator: Stijn De Schepper, Tristan Cordier, Katrine Sandnes Skaar, Jessica Louise Ray, Henrik Sadatzki, Bjørg Risebrobakken
pmc-13549946.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Today, the sea ice cover is rapidly declining in the Arctic Ocean. While major changes in the Arctic marine ecosystems are starting to appear, the full implication of a changing Arctic ecosystem is not well understood. Here we show, using sedimentary ancient DNA metabarcoding to document marine eukaryotic communities, that higher diversity is recorded in a warmer, sea ice free Labrador Sea compared to when this region is sea ice covered.
